questions.question: When driving, what should you do?

options.text: Hide your intentions from other drivers.
Use turn signals only when other vehicles are nearby.
Do not use turn signals in construction zones.
Always use turn signals to tell others what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use turn signals to tell others what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: You must tell other drivers your plans. Signal before you turn or change lanes, even if no other cars are nearby.

questions.question: When using a turn signal, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Turn off the signal after the turn is done.
Leave the signal on long after you finish turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the signal on long after you finish turning.
questions.explanation: Signal early before you turn or change lanes. Keep the signal on until you finish the turn, then turn it off. Do not leave it on after you are done, or you will confuse other drivers.

questions.question: What should you do with the trailer hand valve?

options.text: Use it only when parking downhill.
Use it only when carrying cargo.

questions.explanation: Do not use the trailer hand valve for parking. It can cause air to leak from the brake system, which releases the brakes. Use the parking brake instead.

questions.question: When entering or crossing traffic with a large vehicle, what is most important?

options.text: Make sure there is enough space for your vehicle.
Expect other drivers to make room for you.
Wait for other drivers to wave you in.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure there is enough space for your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need more space than other vehicles. You must have a big enough gap in traffic to enter or cross safely.

questions.question: What must truck tractors with air brakes built after March 1, 1997 have?
questions.explanation: All truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).

questions.question: What is another name for the service line?
questions.explanation: The service line is also called the control line or signal line. It sends air to the trailer brakes. You control it with the foot brake or trailer hand brake.

questions.question: Most heavy-duty vehicles use ____ air brake systems.
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems.

questions.question: What can happen if the fifth wheel plate is not greased properly?
questions.explanation: If the fifth wheel plate is not greased, friction builds up between the tractor and trailer. This causes steering problems.

questions.question: Is emergency equipment, such as a fire extinguisher, required?

options.text: Only for vehicles carrying hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: All commercial vehicles must have proper emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three reflective triangles or flares, and at least one charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: If a trailer starts to skid, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If your trailer skids while braking, release the brakes. This lets the wheels grip the road again. Once the wheels have traction, the trailer will straighten out and follow the tractor.

questions.question: A trailer brake hand valve can be used to:

options.text: Stop the vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop.
questions.explanation: A trailer brake hand valve stops the vehicle from rolling backward when you start from a stop.

questions.question: An automatic tractor protection valve will pop out when:

options.text: Air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi.
Wheels regain traction after a skid.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi.
questions.explanation: The automatic tractor protection valve pops out when air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. This closes the valve and stops air from flowing.

questions.question: During a trip, which shut-off valves should be open?

options.text: All shut-off valves should be open.
Only the rear shut-off valves should be open.
All shut-off valves should be open, except the rear shut-off valves.
No shut-off valves should be open.

questions.correctAnswerText: All shut-off valves should be open, except the rear shut-off valves.
questions.explanation: Keep all shut-off valves open except the last valves on the rear trailer. This lets air reach all brakes and prevents air from escaping the back of the vehicle.

questions.question: Besides reading the manual, the best way to learn about transporting hazardous materials is to:
questions.explanation: The manual helps you pass the written test but doesn't cover all job safety information. Hazardous materials training courses teach you more.

questions.question: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement is needed to transport hazardous materials in:
questions.explanation: You need a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to transport hazardous materials in any sized vehicle.

questions.question: A material's hazard class shows:

options.text: Where items can be placed on the trailer.
How to load and unload the material.

questions.explanation: There are nine hazard classes. Each class shows the risks of that material.

questions.question: If a heavy load is slowing you down, you should:

options.text: Keep the vehicle in second gear.

questions.explanation: The right lanes are for slower traffic. If a heavy load slows you down, stay in the right lane.

questions.question: If a tire rim is damaged, it should be:

options.text: Put on the farthest axle from the driver.

questions.explanation: Wheels or rims with welding repairs are not safe and must be replaced.

questions.question: At dawn or dusk, you can make your vehicle more visible by:
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights at dawn, dusk, and in rain or snow so other drivers can see you.

questions.question: When transporting chlorine, what must you keep in the vehicle?

options.text: A phone with emergency numbers programmed

questions.explanation: Drivers transporting chlorine must keep an approved gas mask and an emergency kit in the vehicle.
